title: CleanBC Roadmap to 2030
summary: Released 25 October 2021. Sets the provincial sectoral pathways to BC's 2030 target. Still the operative provincial plan as of August 2026.
ocUse: The provincial target OC's own reduction pathway has to sit inside. Sets the sectoral ceilings for buildings, transport and industry that constrain what OC can claim.

title: CleanBC Roadmap to 2030: Local Government summary
summary: Two-page local-government framing of the Roadmap, including the funding and planning supports available to local bodies.
ocUse: Short enough to attach to a briefing note. Useful for explaining provincial direction to a non-technical audience.

title: 2025 Progress Report on the 2030 Emissions Reduction Plan
verification: Source read off an official index page, file not opened
summary: Catalogue En4-460/1-2025E-PDF, iv plus 243 pages, issued March 2026. Supersedes the 2023 progress report. The most recent federal progress assessment.
ocUse: Shows whether the national trajectory is on track, which is the honest framing for any OC target that references federal ambition.

title: Canada's 2035 Nationally Determined Contribution
summary: Submitted to UNFCCC 11 February 2025. Commits Canada to 45 to 50 percent below 2005 levels by 2035, roughly 381 to 419 Mt CO2e, as a step toward net zero by 2050. Canada's current NDC and a progression from the 40 to 45 percent 2030 target.
ocUse: The newest federal commitment, and the top of the domestic target ladder. Use this rather than the 2030 NDC when the plan's horizon runs past 2030.

title: 2030 Emissions Reduction Plan
verification: Source read off an official index page, file not opened
summary: Environment and Climate Change Canada, March 2022. Catalogue En4-460/2022E-PDF. The federal sectoral plan underpinning the 2030 commitment.
ocUse: Federal context for the target ladder. Rarely cited directly by an institution, but sets the national trajectory OC's numbers roll up into.

title: Canada's 2021 Nationally Determined Contribution
summary: Submitted to UNFCCC 12 July 2021. The 40 to 45 percent below 2005 by 2030 commitment. Superseded as Canada's latest NDC by the 2035 submission but still the operative 2030 pledge.
ocUse: The internationally registered 2030 number. Use this rather than a news figure when stating Canada's commitment.

title: Canadian Net-Zero Emissions Accountability Act
summary: S.C. 2021 c.22, assented 29 June 2021, consolidation current to 17 June 2026. The source URL always serves the newest consolidation, so this copy will drift from the live statute.
ocUse: The legal architecture behind the 2050 target. Cite the statute rather than a policy document when the plan asserts a legislated obligation.

title: IPCC AR6 Synthesis Report: Summary for Policymakers
verification: Source read off an official index page, file not opened
summary: 2023. The consolidated Sixth Assessment findings in policymaker form. Published as a standalone PDF.
ocUse: The defensible source for any statement about warming trajectories or remaining carbon budgets in the plan's opening case.

title: IPCC AR6 Working Group I: Summary for Policymakers
verification: Source read off an official index page, file not opened
summary: 2021. The physical science basis in policymaker form. This copy matches the SPM extract rather than the longer cover-wrapped standalone edition.
ocUse: Source for regional climate projections framing, which feeds the physical-risk side of Financial and Risk Realities.

title: Decision 1/CP.21, Adoption of the Paris Agreement
summary: Document symbol FCCC/CP/2015/10/Add.1. The COP21 decision with the Agreement annexed.
ocUse: The formal citation for how the Agreement was adopted. Needed only where a document has to be cited precisely.

title: Paris Agreement, full text
summary: The standalone Agreement text, Articles 1 to 29, adopted 12 December 2015. Sixteen pages.
ocUse: The top rung of the target ladder. Quote Article 2 rather than paraphrasing 'the Paris target'.

title: Climate Resilient Kelowna Strategy
summary: September 2024. Targets 40 percent below 2007 by 2030 and net zero by 2050, across 10 drivers, 27 strategies and 153 actions. Supersedes Kelowna's 2018 to 2023 Community Climate Action Plan, whose URL now redirects here.
ocUse: The community inventory boundary OC Kelowna sits inside, and the closest municipal target OC's Kelowna campus will be measured against by neighbours.

title: Corporate Strategic Energy Management Plan
summary: Final report January 2023, 47 pages. Targets a 40 percent corporate GHG cut below 2007 by 2030 and a 20 percent energy-intensity cut below 2012. NOTE: the City calls this the Corporate STRATEGIC Energy Management Plan; the filename says Sustainable.
ocUse: A same-city corporate SEMP with an energy-intensity KPI, directly comparable to what OC needs for its own building portfolio.

title: Penticton Corporate Energy and Emissions Plan
summary: May 2022, roughly 95 pages. Targets a 30 percent corporate GHG cut by 2025 and 45 percent by 2030 against a 2009 baseline. Not linked from the City's climate action page.
ocUse: A recent corporate energy plan from an OC campus city, with explicit interim and 2030 targets against a fixed baseline.

title: Penticton Community Climate Action Plan
summary: October 2021, with appendices A to G. Prepared with the Community Energy Association, part-funded by FortisBC and Emotive.
ocUse: Community context for OC Penticton, and a model of a plan built with external funding partners.

title: Penticton Corporate Climate Action Plan
summary: January 2011, Stantec, under the South Okanagan Similkameen Climate Action Planning Project. Functionally superseded by the 2022 Corporate Energy and Emissions Plan. RISK: the source URL carries no year, so a future corporate plan could silently overwrite it.
ocUse: Historical baseline showing how far municipal practice has moved in fifteen years. Useful for framing OC's own starting point honestly.

title: Salmon Arm Climate Projections technical memorandum
summary: Prepared for the Salmon Arm Climate Resiliency Plan, current source version dated 11 April 2025. VERSIONED SOURCE: the City re-issues this memo at the same URL, so confirm which revision this copy is.
ocUse: Regional climate projections for the Shuswap, feeding the physical-risk assessment for OC Salmon Arm.

title: Salmon Arm GHG Emissions Modelling technical memorandum
summary: Current source version issued 24 October 2025, previous issue 31 July 2025. VERSIONED SOURCE: confirm which revision this copy is. Companion documents exist at the same source, including a Hazard Risk and Vulnerability Analysis.
ocUse: Community and corporate emissions modelling for the smallest OC campus city.

title: Salmon Arm Climate Action Report
summary: Submitted to the Province 5 May 2021. UNLISTED SOURCE: not linked from the City's current climate page, reachable only by its document-centre ID.
ocUse: Municipal reporting context for OC Salmon Arm, and another case where the library copy is the reliable one.

title: Vernon Local Government Climate Action Program survey and attestation
impactAreas: Performance Measurement; Policy / Planning; Carbon Zero
summary: Signed and submitted 31 July 2024, reporting on the 2023 calendar year. The reporting year is not printed on a cover page; it appears in the question wording, which asks about emissions measured 'for the 2023 calendar year'. Vernon's own stated targets in this submission are 50 percent by 2030, 75 percent by 2040 and 100 percent by 2050, all steeper than the provincial 40 / 60 / 80 legislated targets.
ocUse: Shows the provincial survey-and-attestation format local governments file, a useful comparator to OC's own CCAR template. More usefully, it records a neighbouring municipality voluntarily committing beyond the provincial target, which is a relevant reference point when OC sets its own ambition.

title: City of Vernon Climate Action Plan
summary: April 2021. FLAG: Vernon opened a review of this plan in early 2026, so it may be superseded shortly.
ocUse: Municipal context for OC Vernon. Watch for the refreshed version before citing targets.

title: Vernon GHG Emissions Modelling and Reduction Targets Report
summary: February 2020. 2017 baseline of 309,407 tCO2e, split 63 percent transport, 26 percent natural gas, 7 percent waste. ORPHANED SOURCE: no longer linked from any current City page, found by search only.
ocUse: A worked municipal modelling method, and a cautionary case for why the library copy matters. The source could disappear without notice.

title: BCIT Electric Vehicles program area

title: BCIT ZEB microcredential catalogue
summary: Wind Turbine Essentials, Renewable Energy Electrical Systems, Renewable Energy Fundamentals for Electricians, Intro to Photovoltaics, Net-Zero and Passive House Construction, Mass Timber Construction.

title: Zero Energy Emissions Buildings Learning Centre ZEBLC
summary: Microcredential hub training trades professionals in net-zero design, retrofits, BC Energy Step Code and Passive House. Flagship: a Residential Air-to-Air Heat Pump Specialist microcredential, 90-100% tuition-subsidized through Mar 2027. Funded by BC Housing, BC Hydro, Vancity, REFBC and FortisBC.

title: BCIT STARS Report Silver
summary: Silver, valid to Oct 2027. The large polytechnic with the trades focus most comparable to OC's mandate.

title: Envisioning 2030 strategic plan

title: Illuminating 2030 Academic Plan Summary
summary: A 10-year academic plan that explicitly names climate in crisis as a challenge the university must address, alongside land and place-based learning and Indigenous reconciliation.
ocUse: Model for embedding sustainability into an academic plan rather than only an operational one. Relevant to OC's Academics focus area.

title: Climate Change Accountability Report 2025
summary: 1,889 tCO2e, 13.4% below the 2010 baseline but up 17.1% year over year. 94% of emissions are stationary building energy. Offsets cost $45,348. The new Fulmer Family Centre targets LEED Gold and is fully electric.
ocUse: A cautionary data point: a Silver-STARS institution with an active energy plan still posted a year-over-year emissions increase. Useful for setting non-linear, honest OC targets.

title: Sustainability Goals Are We On Track progress review
summary: Reports a 10-year Campus Energy and Emissions Plan target of 50% below 2007 by 2030, delayed by COVID. 73% of students use sustainable commuting per a 2024 survey. U-Pass BC and carpool incentives in place. A $1.5M NSERC Mobilize climate-research grant in 2023.
ocUse: The 73% sustainable-commute figure is a strong TDM benchmark. Also a model of public accountability tracking against stated targets.

title: STARS Report Silver 55.02
summary: STARS Silver, 55.02 points, submitted 2 July 2024, valid to 8 Aug 2027.
ocUse: An active Silver rating at a teaching-focused multi-campus peer. A realistic first-target benchmark alongside UFV and UNBC.

title: Squamish MOU 13 Collaboration Areas
summary: A multi-campus town-gown MOU including a dedicated climate-action commitment, a circular-economy commitment with 1.25 FTE faculty time and about $16,500, and an Indigenous partnership tied to the Atl'ka7tsem/Howe Sound Biosphere Region Society.
ocUse: Template for formalizing sustainability MOUs with Kelowna, Vernon, Salmon Arm and Penticton. Directly analogous multi-campus town-gown structure.

title: Applied Coastal Ecology Environmental Geoscience diplomas
summary: Place-based environmental science diplomas. No institution-wide sustainability plan, STARS rating or climate targets found.
ocUse: A curriculum-only sustainability posture. A useful contrast to OC's integrated four-pillar approach.

title: CNC Strategic Plan #CNCNext50
summary: No sustainability, climate or environmental goals surfaced in the institutional strategic plan. A CNC CCAR exists via the provincial index.
ocUse: A negative benchmark showing how far ahead a published four-pillar plan already puts OC.

title: Sustainability and Climate Action Plan townhall draft
summary: A Climate Action Task Force established Fall 2020 presented a draft Sustainability and Climate Action Plan after more than two years of consultation. No finalized plan was locatable.
ocUse: A stakeholder-townhall consultation format OC could mirror. Note the plan itself is not confirmed published.

title: Climate Change Accountability Report 2025
summary: 176 tCO2e, fully offset at $4,400. Actions include lighting and HVAC scheduling optimization, metering recalibration, EV charging, and a planned 2026 propane-to-electric forklift swap.
ocUse: A minimum-viable CCAR at single-campus scale. Least transferable to OC's 45 buildings, useful mainly as a floor comparator.

title: Climate Action at ECU update
summary: Task force formed Fall 2020 in response to student activism and Senate discussion. Student Climate Action Network established 2019. No numeric targets.
ocUse: A governance-process example only. Advocacy-oriented rather than metrics-driven.

title: Emergency and Disaster Management programs
summary: Formal disaster and emergency management credentials. Institutional capacity directly relevant to climate-resilience training.
ocUse: A potential curriculum partner if OC ever builds climate-emergency content into trades or general education.

title: Climate Change Accountability Report 2025
summary: 742 tCO2e, up 4% year over year. A Strategic Energy Management Plan targets a 44% energy-use cut by 2029/30 against 2008/09. Critically, JIBC conducts wildfire-smoke and extreme-heat vulnerability and HVAC-filtration assessments, with a full climate vulnerability assessment planned for 2026.
ocUse: The best physical-climate-adaptation model found anywhere in this project. A direct template for a wildfire-smoke and extreme-heat HVAC resilience assessment across OC's four Interior campuses. Serves target T4.

title: STARS Report Bronze 32.33
summary: STARS Bronze, 32.33 points, submitted 25 Sept 2025, valid to 20 Oct 2028. Strongest category was Air and Climate at 9.98 of 11.
ocUse: The lowest active rating in the BC set. Useful as the realistic floor for a first scored submission, and shows a resilience focus scores well in Air and Climate.

title: KPU Electric Vehicle Maintenance Training
summary: Another BC EV technician offering in automotive trades.
ocUse: Third data point confirming EV-tech training is now standard in BC. Benchmark curriculum hours and cost against all three.

title: KPU Sustainable Food Systems and Security programs
summary: Signature sustainable agriculture and food security programming.
ocUse: The clear BC academic partner if OC builds a food-systems or local-procurement angle.

title: KPU Sustainability Report 2023 2024
summary: Annual public report separate from STARS and CCAR filings.
ocUse: Template for an annual public report distinct from the regulatory filing.

title: KPU Sustainability Framework KPU2050
summary: Sustainability as one of five institutional strategic goals. An Office of Sustainability plus a cross-departmental Sustainability Hub. SDG Accord and Race to Zero signatory. Silver STARS (2024).
ocUse: The Sustainability Hub cross-departmental model is a strong Operational Dependencies template, mirroring OC's Procurement/IT/Facilities coordination need.

title: Indigenous Leading Practices Community Based Assessment
summary: NVIT's culturally responsive Community Based Assessment service, Elder-led openings, strength-based feedback and individualized plans, serving 900+ students across 50+ communities since 2011.
ocUse: A governance and process model for embedding Indigenous protocols into institutional service delivery. Relevant to OC's Layer 0 even though it is not an environmental document.

title: Climate Change Accountability Report 2025
summary: 274 tCO2e plus 534 t biogenic reported separately, offsets $6,700. Geothermal serves six buildings, a heat pump serves a 900 sq ft academic building, six Level 2 EV chargers installed, a Clean Fleet Plan in development, and plans to electrify Mobile Training Labs to eliminate diesel generators.
ocUse: Geothermal and heat-pump portfolio model, plus the idea of electrifying mobile training labs. Directly applicable to OC's own mobile trades assets.

title: Centre of Excellence in Sustainability building
summary: A 19,500 sq ft purpose-built teaching building with a live geothermal system, rooftop PV, and an educational solar array with three tilt and orientation configurations for hands-on student testing. Houses trades labs, gym, greenhouse and commercial kitchen.
ocUse: The strongest living-lab building model found. Instrumented, visible building systems used as teaching tools. Directly transferable to an OC trades building retrofit and to the Four-Campus Living Lab initiative.

title: NIC SPARK initiative unverified

ocUse: Flagged as a lead only. Follow up directly with NIC before citing.

title: NIC Comox campus solar installation

title: Centre for Applied Energy and Environmental Sustainability CAEES

title: Royal Roads Climate Action Plan 2022 2027
summary: Net-zero campus by 2050 with 65% cut by 2025 and 80% by 2030. Four commitments: community engagement and living labs, climate resilience, mitigation/adaptation pilots, curriculum integration. Race to Zero participant.
ocUse: A clean staged-percentage GHG target ladder (65% to 80% to net zero) directly reusable for OC's Carbon Zero roadmap.

title: Selkirk College Sustainability Plan 2023 2027
summary: Four-pillar plan (Academics/Research, Engagement, Operations, Planning & Admin), near-identical to OC's four focus areas. 60% building GHG cut below 2010 by 2027, net-zero by 2030 pledge, 20% increase in sustainability-defined courses.
ocUse: The closest structural mirror to OC's own framework in the college sector. Benchmark pillar definitions and KPI style almost 1:1.

title: UNBC AASHE STARS Reports Gold 68.83
summary: Gold, 68.83, achieved Mar 6 2026, valid to Apr 2029. Up from Silver (56.09) in 2011. The best currently-active rating in the cohort.
ocUse: The best-in-cohort active benchmark. A 15-year Silver-to-Gold trajectory is a realistic curve for OC's T3.

title: UNBC Sustainability Strategic Plan 2025 2035 draft v5.1
summary: New 10-year plan, explicitly a living document with annual progress reporting. Sustainability Office relaunched Jan 2024.
ocUse: The newest full sustainability strategic plan in the BC non-research-university cohort. Worth a deep read given OC is drafting in the same window.

title: UNBC Bioenergy Plant Canada's Green University
summary: Wood-pellet bioenergy plant heating campus, anchoring a trademarked green-university brand position.
ocUse: Branding lesson: one flagship asset can anchor an entire external identity. A model for elevating Trades for the Transition the same way.

title: VIU Sustainability Initiatives
summary: Gamified behaviour-change campaigns: Space Heater Defeaters, Active Transportation Bingo, Energy Dance.
ocUse: Low-cost, high-visibility campaign formats for OC's Engagement focus area.

title: VIU Position Statement on Climate Action and Sustainability

title: Camosun Climate Pathways V4

title: Camosun STARS Report page

summary: Thin public content. States the Strategic Plan includes initiatives toward a zero-carbon future but publishes no targets or plan document.

title: Douglas College STARS Report Silver 46.21

title: Langara STARS Report Silver 51.63
